title: Donated Services & Noncash Contributions
description: Determine when donated services and other contributed nonfinancial assets should be recognized.
html:
Donated Services

Not-for-profit organizations often receive services from volunteers.

However, donated services are not automatically recognized as contribution revenue and expense.

When Are Donated Services Recognized?

Donated services are generally recognized when they meet certain criteria.

  • The services create or enhance a nonfinancial asset.
  • OR the services require specialized skills, are provided by individuals possessing those skills, and would typically need to be purchased if they were not donated.
DONATED SERVICE RECOGNIZE IF: CREATES / ENHANCES NONFINANCIAL ASSET OR SPECIALIZED SKILL + PROVIDED BY SKILLED PERSON + OTHERWISE WOULD BE PURCHASED

Specialized Skills

Specialized skills may include services provided by professionals such as:

Lawyers Specialized Skill
Accountants Specialized Skill
Doctors Specialized Skill
Electricians Specialized Skill

Example — Donated Legal Services

Example

An attorney donates legal services with a fair value of $12,000.

The NFP would otherwise have hired an attorney to perform the work.

Contribution Revenue = $12,000 Legal Expense = $12,000

The NFP recognizes both contribution revenue and the related expense.

Example — Volunteer Reception Work

Assume volunteers provide general reception and clerical support.

If the services do not require specialized skills and do not create or enhance a nonfinancial asset, they generally are not recognized.

GENERAL VOLUNTEER SERVICE DOES NOT MEET CRITERIA → NO RECOGNITION

Services That Create a Nonfinancial Asset

Donated services may also be recognized if they create or enhance a nonfinancial asset.

Example

Skilled workers donate labor to construct a new facility for an NFP.

Because the services create a nonfinancial asset, the value of the donated services may generally be capitalized as part of the asset.

Noncash Contributions

Not-for-profit organizations may also receive contributed nonfinancial assets rather than cash.

Examples

  • Food
  • Clothing
  • Equipment
  • Land
  • Building materials
  • Pharmaceuticals

Measurement

Contributed nonfinancial assets are generally measured at fair value when recognized.

CONTRIBUTED NONFINANCIAL ASSET → FAIR VALUE

Example — Donated Equipment

A donor gives an NFP equipment with a fair value of $40,000.

Assume there are no donor restrictions.

Equipment + $40,000 Contribution Revenue + $40,000

Donor Restrictions Still Matter

A donated noncash asset may still be subject to donor-imposed restrictions.

For example, donated land may be restricted for use only as a community garden.

NONCASH CONTRIBUTION + DONOR RESTRICTION → NET ASSETS WITH DONOR RESTRICTIONS

Donated Services vs. Donated Goods

Donated Services Recognize Only If Criteria Are Met
Donated Goods Generally Recognize at Fair Value When Recognized

Example — Medical Supplies

A health charity receives donated medical supplies with a fair value of $25,000.

If the contribution is unconditional and unrestricted:

Supplies = $25,000 Contribution Revenue = $25,000

CPA Memory Rule

DONATED SERVICE? ASK: SPECIALIZED? WOULD WE OTHERWISE BUY IT? OR DOES IT CREATE A NONFINANCIAL ASSET? YES → RECOGNIZE NO → GENERALLY DON'T RECOGNIZE

Key Takeaways

  • Not all volunteer services are recognized.
  • Specialized donated services may be recognized when they would otherwise need to be purchased.
  • Services creating or enhancing nonfinancial assets may also be recognized.
  • Contributed nonfinancial assets are generally measured at fair value.
  • Donor restrictions can affect the net asset classification of noncash contributions.

quiz.prompt: A CPA donates audit services to an NFP. The services have a fair value of $18,000, require specialized accounting skills, and the NFP would otherwise have hired a CPA to perform the work. How should the NFP generally account for the donated services?

choices.text: Do not recognize the services because no cash was paid
Recognize $18,000 of contribution revenue and $18,000 of related expense
Recognize the amount directly as net assets with donor restrictions

quiz.explanation: The donated services require specialized skills, are provided by someone possessing those skills, and would otherwise need to be purchased. Therefore, the NFP generally recognizes both contribution revenue and the related expense at fair value.

objectives: Explain donated services & noncash contributions and its underlying principles.
Apply the topic to a financial-reporting scenario.
